answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce, slashable stake before submitting jobs or claiming rewards. If an agent double-spends or violates rules, part of its stake is burned. Splitting funds across many identities does not multiply the attacker’s capital: each Sybil needs its own stake, tied up and at risk. The mechanism creates an oasis of trusted activity along a ridge of costly participation, with every extra identity adding a ledge of capital to fund and potentially lose.
